executive_summary.question: Under the BSA, are facts inconsistent with a fact in issue, or that make the existence of a fact in issue highly probable or improbable, relevant even if not otherwise relevant?
executive_summary.generated_answer:
Yes. Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), facts that are **inconsistent with a fact in issue** or that **make the existence or non‑existence of a fact in issue highly probable or improbable** are deemed relevant **even if they would not otherwise be relevant**.

This is expressly provided in **Section 9** of the BSA:

> **9. Facts not otherwise relevant are relevant—**  
> **(1) if they are inconsistent with any fact in issue or relevant fact;**  
> **(2) if by themselves or in connection with other facts they make the existence or non‑existence of any fact in issue or relevant fact highly probable or improbable.**  

[Chunk-ID: 1f44cb03-d12a-41ef-940b-49a1848dd6ec]  

Thus, such facts are admissible as relevant evidence under the BSA.
